services.title: You do not need to know which service to ask for.
services.intro: Choose the starting point that sounds most like your situation. LDW can map it to the right website, systems, ownership, or consulting work after a short conversation.

startingPoints.title: I need a better website.
startingPoints.description: The site may be dated, hard to maintain, unclear, or simply not doing enough for the business.

startingPoints.title: We waste time doing this manually — or our tools don't work together.
startingPoints.description: A repeated workflow, handoff, or disconnected toolset may be a better fit for configuration, integration, automation, or a focused internal tool.

startingPoints.title: I'm not sure what we own, what we need, or what should change.
startingPoints.description: When ownership, vendors, platforms, costs, or the right next step are unclear, start with a practical review before buying or rebuilding anything.

ownership.title: Your business should own its digital assets.
ownership.lede: Domains, DNS, website and hosting accounts, repositories, cloud services, business profiles, and other critical systems should be held in business-controlled primary accounts wherever practical.
items: MFA and recovery responsibility made explicit

process.title: Assess → Improve or Build → Handoff or Care

steps.title: Assess
steps.description: Understand the real need, current systems, constraints, ownership, risk, and cost before choosing technology.

steps.title: Improve or build
steps.description: Keep useful systems when possible. Configure, integrate, automate, or build only what the problem actually requires.

steps.title: Handoff or care
steps.description: Leave clear ownership and documentation, then continue with bounded ongoing care only when it creates useful value.

contact.eyebrow: Start with what is not working

faq.title: A few things you should know before reaching out.

items.question: Do I need to know which LDW service I need?
items.answer: No. Start with the problem, what is happening today, and what you want to improve. LDW can map that to website, systems, ownership, or consulting work after a short conversation.

items.question: Will LDW try to replace the tools we already use?
items.answer: Not by default. Existing platforms and native capabilities are reviewed first. Configuration, integration, and maintained services are preferred when they solve the problem well; custom work is reserved for a real gap.

items.question: Who owns the website, code, cloud accounts, and other business assets after the work?
items.answer: Customer-owned production assets are the default where practical. LDW generally works through named, scoped access and documents deployment, recovery, handoff, and rollback so ownership stays understandable.

items.question: Can LDW provide ongoing help after a project?
items.answer: Yes, when an agreed maintenance or administration scope creates useful value. Ongoing care is bounded and does not require giving up ownership of the underlying business assets.
